content:
One of my favorite iPhone cases is back with a new look. I've used BitmoLab's previous generations of the GAMEBABY case, and I loved it from the moment I tried it. It feels like an accessory designed specifically to trigger my sense of nostalgia. The biggest selling point of this case is that it's not an accessory that needs to be carried separately and kept charged—it's a cleverly designed regular iPhone case that also features physical buttons, letting you play your favorite Game Boy ROMs (and other games). It's a perfect example of "working smart, not hard." It requires no battery or Bluetooth, and setup is incredibly simple. If you're a fan of any type of retro game emulator, you'll definitely want to keep an eye on this product.

Check out our case hands-on video!

This case has a simple yet ingenious design. It uses a two-piece design, with the lower half serving as a controller. For everyday non-gaming use, it feels just like a regular case. You get:

  • Tactile side buttons for the lock key, volume keys, and action key
  • Cutouts for the USB-C port, speakers, buttons, and camera controls
  • A protective lip surrounding the screen and camera base
  • Hard-shell plastic protection

But the magic is all in the lower half. The game's control buttons are right there, and they're beautifully made, with a satisfying tactile feel when pressed. But how exactly does it work?

How It Works

Again, the brilliance of this product is that there are no electronic components inside, so no pairing is required. How it works is that each physical game button is equipped with a small capacitive contact point that mimics the effect of your finger touching the screen. As a result, the iPhone thinks you're tapping the on-screen control keys, while you feel the feedback of a real button. It's the same technology used in the soft capacitive tips on cheap styluses.

There's a simple setup step to ensure the physical buttons align with the on-screen control keys. BitmoLabs provides all the necessary instructions via a QR code on the packaging. It works through the Delta Emulator app on the App Store. The app is completely free, with absolutely no in-app purchases. After downloading the app, GAMEBABY provides a downloadable custom interface that places the emulator's virtual control keys directly beneath the physical buttons. This is also free (you can use it even if you don't have the case).

Once the interface is installed in the Delta Emulator app, you can start playing. You simply detach the lower half of the case, flip it over, and reattach it to the iPhone. This aligns the control buttons with the iPhone screen, giving you a genuine physical button experience while playing retro games. When you're done gaming, just slide out the controller portion, flip it over, and snap it back into place to return to regular case mode.

User Experience

As I mentioned at the beginning, I have absolutely no resistance to any retro gaming element—it touches something deep inside me and makes me want to revisit Pokémon games from years ago. This case not only makes the gameplay easier, but it also delivers an experience with virtually no friction. No need to remember to bring extra items, no charging required, and no pairing needed. For me, remembering to bring all the necessary accessories is often the biggest barrier to using tech accessories, and this case eliminates exactly that obstacle.

Additionally, you can tell that BitmoLabs has significantly improved the build quality with this case. The button feedback is excellent, bouncing back when released, and I experienced no unresponsive buttons during gameplay. I primarily used it to revisit all the classic Pokémon titles, which are relatively casual games that don't demand quick reflexes. Even for games that do require fast reactions, this case can handle it.

There's one trade-off worth noting: no MagSafe support. Since the case has a two-piece design and the lower half already takes up space, there's simply no room to add MagSafe functionality. So, if you absolutely must use a MagSafe case, this product might not be for you. That said, if you have MagSafe accessories (I personally have quite a few), you just need to take the case off to use them—it's a very simple process. Also, this case doesn't have a camera control cover, which isn't a big deal, but it's worth noting.

Pricing and Availability

GAMEBABY is available on the BitmoLab official website and Amazon, starting at $24.99. Three versions are offered: GameBaby Color, GameBaby Retro, and the latest GameBaby Transparent (the one I'm showing here). GameBaby Transparent is only compatible with the iPhone 17 Pro Max, and production is limited to 500 units, available exclusively on the BitmoLab official website. The other versions are compatible with the iPhone 15 Pro and newer models, and are available on both Amazon and the official website. Again, since there are no electronic components, batteries, or Bluetooth inside, they've been able to keep the price down to $25, which is an absolute bargain for a case!

Conclusion

If you're like me and love revisiting retro games on your iPhone, this case is the perfect choice. It's affordable, lightweight and portable, simple to set up, and genuinely enhances the experience of playing retro emulated games on the iPhone. Pairing physical buttons with the iPhone's excellent haptic engine creates the sensation of actually playing a retro gaming console. With a recent wave of retro Pokémon game mods popping up all over my social media lately, now is the perfect time to relax and enjoy these games on your iPhone with physical buttons.

What are your thoughts on this case? Would you consider getting one? Have you tried it before? Feel free to discuss in the comments below!
